neutral_facts.value: The accused attacked the victims, who were in a car, with sharp and deadly weapons, including swords, baseball bats, and daatars. The assailants smashed the car's glass and inflicted grievous injuries on the victims. Medical reports confirmed that the injuries were caused by sharp-edged weapons. The Special Investigation Team recovered weapons and vehicles used in the attack, and CCTV footage was examined. The prosecution alleged that the attack was carried out with the intention to kill the victims, as evidenced by the attackers' statements and the nature of the injuries inflicted.

appeal_history.value: Trial court: Charge framed under Section 307 IPC; High Court: Deleted charge under Section 307 IPC; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed, High Court order quashed and set aside

quotes.text: The Sessions Judge framed charges under the aforesaid provisions, including Section 307 IPC. This order of framing of charge was challenged by respondent No. 2 by filing revision petition in the High Court.

The High Court has, vide the impugned judgment dated 28.08.2015, partly allowed the said revision petition and deleted the charge framed under Section 307 IPC as unsustainable while maintaining the charge in respect of other offences.
Resultantly, this appeal is allowed and the order of the High Court is hereby quashed and set aside.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused persons, armed with deadly weapons, attacked the victims in a car, causing grievous injuries, and that the ingredients of Section 307 IPC were made out.

quotes.text: According to the appellant, who is a practicing Advocate enrolled with the Bar Counsel of Punjab, he was brutally attacked on I 0.05.2004 with intention to kill him, his brother, Avnish Mahajan, and their employee, Avtar Singh, by 10-12 persons, who were armed with sharp and deadly weapons including Gandassa, daatars, baseball bat, etc.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the medical evidence did not support the charge under Section 307 IPC and that the intention to kill was conspicuously missing.

quotes.text: medical evidence available on record does not support the charge under Section 307 IPC and at the most, charge would be made only under Section 326 IPC.
intention to kill was conspicuously missing which is sine qua non of charge under Section 307 IPC.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that the intention to kill or knowledge that death will be caused is a question of fact to be determined based on the evidence, and that injuries need not be on the fatal part of the body to attract Section 307 IPC.

quotes.text: In order to attract the provisions of Section 307 IPC, injury need not be on fatal part of the body.

the question as to whether there was an intention to kill or knowledge that death will be caused is a question of fact and would depend on the facts of a given case which has to be attributed on evidence by the trial court.
